threads.thread_goal: Align on campaign objectives, audiences and key messages before content creation.

messages.text: Team, let's kick off the 'Corporate Safety & Sustainability Awareness Campaign'. I've started drafting the core document, A1 Campaign Strategy and Messaging Framework, which will guide our work on T1 and T2. The primary goal is to improve staff awareness across all sites. I've outlined two main audience segments: 1) On-site operational staff and 2) Office-based corporate staff. Please review the draft objectives in A1 and share your thoughts.

Thanks for getting this started. The structure in A1 looks solid. The objectives are clear, but I suggest we add a measurable component to each. For example, for 'improve awareness', could we aim for something like a 15% increase in quiz scores or a 10% reduction in reported minor incidents? This will help us later with the post-campaign evaluation.

This is a great starting point. The audience segmentation makes sense. For T2, it would be helpful to know if we have any data on which channels each group uses most frequently. That will help me prioritize content development for the digital kit.
Excellent point on measurement. I'll add a 'Success Metrics' column to the objectives table in A1. Let's refine those metrics as we define the evaluation framework.

Good question. I believe HR has some past survey data on channel preferences. I'll request it and share. For now, let's assume on-site staff are best reached via signage and team briefings, while office staff engage more with intranet and email.
Hi, which sites are we talking about for the on-site staff? Just the main production facilities or also the smaller warehouses?
For the security messages in T1, we need to be very clear about the rules for wearing ID badges. This is a big problem. We should make it the number one message.

The project brief lists 'all sites', so I'd recommend we plan for a scalable approach that can be adapted for both large and small locations. We can prioritize the main facilities for larger activations.

That's a valid operational point. We can use the ID badge issue as a specific example of 'vigilance' in our materials. However, for the core messages in A1, we need to stay at a higher level, focusing on the principles of safety, security, and sustainability. We can cover specific procedures in the detailed content, especially for T11 where we align on security examples.
Ok I understand. So the main message is the big idea and then we use the badge thing as an example. Got it.
Sounds good, that's enough to get started on the channel strategy for T2.

I've updated A1 with the success metrics column and drafted the three core messages for each pillar: Safety, Security, and Sustainability. They are on page 2. Please take a look and provide any final feedback.
The messages look great. They are simple, memorable, and cover the key themes. I have no further comments.
They work for me. Easy to adapt for different channels.
Looks good.
I approve.
Excellent. With everyone's input, we can now formalize these decisions.

Great. To summarize and close this out: 
1. We approve the campaign objectives and primary audience segments (On-site operational staff, Office-based corporate staff) as defined in A1. 
2. We sign off on the core safety, security, and sustainability key messages, also in A1. 
This concludes T1 and unblocks T2 and T11.

threads.thread_goal: Define the campaign channel mix, calendar and event concepts.

messages.text: Hi team, following our alignment on strategy, I've created a first draft of the A3 Campaign Channel and Event Calendar. It outlines a proposed mix of digital content for T5 and on-site signage for T7. I'd love to get your input, especially on the event concepts for T3. What kind of activations do you think would work best at our main sites?

Thanks! For the events, we could do a big launch event at each of the three main sites. We could have guest speakers, maybe some interactive booths for safety equipment, and provide lunch for everyone who attends. I can start looking into catering vendors for T8.

That's an engaging idea, but we need to be mindful of the limited budget constraint mentioned in the project pack. A full catered event at three sites might be too costly. Could we consider a more scalable 'train-the-trainer' model or smaller, pop-up style info sessions? Also, for any event format we choose for T3, we'll need a risk assessment as part of the definition of done.

I agree with focusing on scalability. The goal is awareness, not a party. How about we reframe the 'event' as an 'activation'? We could have short, 15-minute 'safety huddles' led by local managers at the start of shifts. We can support them with materials from the campaign. This would align well with the core messages in A1 and be very budget-friendly.

Oh, okay. The budget is tight. The pop-up idea could work. We could have a small table in the cafeteria during lunch breaks for a week. I can plan the logistics for that in A5. I will also remember to do the risk assessment.

I love the 'safety huddles' idea. It's authentic and reaches the on-site staff in their own environment. We can create simple, visual talking points for the managers, which ties into T7 for posters. For office staff, we can stick to the digital channels outlined in A3: intranet articles and a targeted email series.
When we put up the posters for T7, we need to make sure they are not in places where they can be easily damaged. The loading dock is a bad spot.
Good practical point. We should add a note in the T7 execution plan to consult with site security on optimal and safe placement for all on-site materials.

Okay, so it sounds like we have a plan. I'll update A3. 
- Digital: Intranet, email series (2x week for 2 weeks). 
- On-site: Posters in high-traffic areas (cafeteria, entrances), plus the 'safety huddle' activations. 
Does this channel mix and frequency work for everyone?
This looks like a targeted and effective plan. I approve.
Yes, I can work with that for the event planning in A5.
The plan is approved. It's realistic and aligns with our constraints. Let's lock it in.
Great. I'm marking these decisions as confirmed. I'll finalize the calendar in A3 by EOD.

threads.thread_goal: Set up and validate the quality and compliance review process for all assets.

messages.text: Team, to ensure all our campaign materials are compliant and high-quality, I've drafted the A2 Quality Review Checklist as part of T4. I've also outlined a proposed review workflow for T9. The goal is a clear, efficient process for getting assets approved. Please review the documents and provide feedback, especially on the checklist items and proposed owners.

This is excellent, very thorough. The checklist in A2 covers all the key areas: legal, safety, brand, and messaging consistency. Given our tight 21-day timeline, what's the proposed SLA for review turnaround? We should define that in the T9 workflow to avoid bottlenecks.

Thanks for putting this together. It's very helpful. In the workflow, can we clarify who the final sign-off is for digital assets versus print? I assume corporate comms needs to give the final blessing on everything, but is there a specific person?

Great question. I propose a 24-hour SLA for initial review and a 48-hour SLA for final sign-off from stakeholders like legal or safety. I'll add this to the T9 document. We can track the status of each asset in the A6 Asset Review Tracker I've just created.

Correct. The comms lead will be the final business approver for all assets. For specific safety/security content, the respective officers must also sign off. I'll add a column in A6 to specify the required approvers for each asset type.
So when I write something I send it to you first? Or to the security manager? I'm not sure about the order.
Does this review process also apply to things like contracts with the event vendors? Sometimes legal takes a while to review those.

Good question for clarification. The process is sequential. You would first do a self-check using A2, then submit it for peer review within this team. After that, it goes to the formal stakeholders (like the security manager) for their sign-off. I'll add a simple flowchart to the T9 doc to make it clearer.

This process is specifically for campaign *content* and *materials*. Vendor contracts follow a separate procurement/legal process. However, any public-facing materials the vendor produces for us *would* need to go through this A2 checklist.
Ok, that makes sense. Thanks.
The SLAs and the tracker in A6 sound perfect. I have no other comments on A2, it's ready from my perspective.
The approver column in A6 is a great idea. The process is clear to me now. I approve the checklist.
Thanks for the feedback, everyone. I've updated the T9 workflow with the SLAs and the flowchart, and updated A6 with the approver column. It sounds like we have consensus.

Let's formalize the decisions: 
1. The final version of the A2 quality review checklist is approved. 
2. We agree on the 24/48h review SLAs and the use of A6 to track sign-offs for each asset type. 
I will now mark T4 as complete and we can begin using this process as per T9.

threads.thread_goal: Align on spokesperson materials, manager briefing guide and FAQs.

messages.text: Hi all, I've drafted the first versions of the A4 Spokesperson Talking Points and Q&A Pack and the A8 Manager Briefing Guide and Employee FAQ. These are for tasks T6 and T12. The content is based directly on our approved messaging framework in A1. I'd appreciate your review for clarity, accuracy, and tone.

Thanks for sharing these so quickly. The documents are clear, well-structured, and perfectly aligned with A1. I've cross-referenced the Q&A in A4 with our compliance checklist and have one minor suggestion: let's add a question to the FAQ in A8 about how employee data from engagement surveys will be used, just to be proactive on privacy.
That's a sharp catch. I completely agree. I'll add that to the FAQ in A8 right away. Thank you.

These look great. For the manager guide A8, could we embed a link to the central intranet page where all the final campaign assets will be stored? It would make it easy for them to find posters and other materials.
Simple and effective idea. Done. I've added a placeholder link to A8.
In the talking points A4 it says 'be vigilant'. We should also say 'report suspicious activity to security immediately using the hotline number'. We need to be specific.

That's a crucial procedural detail. The main talking points in A4 are meant to be high-level, but you're right that managers need to give concrete instructions. I'll add your suggested wording to the 'What to tell your team' section of the manager guide in A8, and make sure it points to the official security protocol document.
Ok thank you.
Will the people hosting the safety huddles get this pack? Or will they get a separate training?

The A8 Manager Briefing Guide is designed specifically for them. It's a self-contained kit to help any manager or supervisor run one of the huddles effectively. We aren't planning a separate live training to keep things scalable.
With the latest changes incorporated, I'm happy to approve both A4 and A8. They are ready for stakeholder review outside this team.
Same here, they look good to go.
Perfect. Thanks for the swift and valuable feedback, everyone. I've made all the suggested updates. We can now consider these approved by the project team.

To confirm: 
1. We are signing off on the A4 spokesperson talking points and Q&A pack. 
2. We are approving the A8 manager briefing guide and FAQ for distribution. 
I will send these for final validation by security and HR leadership today, which completes T6 and T12.

threads.thread_goal: Review launch readiness and define post-campaign measurement approach.

messages.text:
Team, we are approaching our launch date. I've updated the A6 Asset Review Tracker; all assets have now passed the A2 checklist and are approved. The A3 calendar is locked. Based on this, I'm proposing a 'Go' for launch. Please confirm if you agree or have any final blockers. 

Separately, for T10, please review the draft A7 Post-Campaign Evaluation Report Template, which outlines our proposed KPIs. We need to agree on these to ensure we measure success effectively.

Excellent work on getting everything through the review process. I see no blockers. It's a definite 'Go' from me. Reviewing A7 now. The quantitative KPIs (reach, engagement rate) are good. I suggest we add a qualitative KPI: 'Key themes from manager feedback sessions'. This will give us valuable context.

All digital assets are scheduled and ready to go as per A3. I'm a 'Go' for launch. The KPIs in A7 look good. For the 'intranet page views' KPI, is that data coming from our standard analytics dashboard? Just want to confirm the source.
Great suggestion. Qualitative feedback is key for continuous improvement. I'll add that to A7. Thanks.
Yes, that data will be pulled directly from the corporate intranet's analytics dashboard. I've listed the specific data source for each KPI in the appendix of A7.
All logistics for the on-site activations are confirmed. We had a small issue with the banner printing vendor but they confirmed it will be delivered on time. So we are a 'Go'.
Thanks for the update. Glad to hear the vendor issue is resolved. Please keep an eye on it.
I am ready. It is a Go.
Perfect, thanks. The measurement plan in A7 is approved from my side.
It's unanimous then. We have full alignment on launch readiness and the measurement plan.

Let's make it official. 
1. We confirm a 'Go' for the campaign launch based on the completed A6 tracker and readiness checks. 
2. We agree on the KPIs and the 30-day post-campaign evaluation timeline as defined in the updated A7. 
Congratulations team on reaching this milestone!
